data.body: Final rebar-debug report. Problem: the existential Pandoc corpus witness was an individual CI long pole despite asserting only existence. Proven root cause: the test exhausted all eligible prose units after both witnesses already existed. Runtime proof on the real renderer measured 232 calls / 8.865s versus 1 call / 0.036s with exact witness evaluation, saving 231 subprocesses and 8.829s locally. Test proof: a strengthened held-out oracle was RED before repair (`render_calls` 232 versus first changed call 1); the fixer did not see it; the repaired code was GREEN in 0.47s; deleting both exits reseeded the exact defect and returned RED (`232 != 1`); restoring them returned GREEN. Forced identity-renderer and no-eligible controls both still fail. Fix: change 1759 / merged commit 67765041c810d094ddaf479cf5448a3897b475c8 adds inner and outer exits immediately after a real `_render_unit` output changes, retaining `_lock_and_split`, the real Pandoc boundary, and both existential assertions. Scope and safety: test-only change; no product path or dependency changed; no assertion was removed or weakened; full-corpus safety/richness/fixed-point consumers of `corpus_pass1` are untouched. Focused CI-equivalent module: 11 passed in 27.22s; existential call duration 0.04s. Construct sweep: no second `_render_unit` existential loop exists; the distinct legacy-oracle duplication remains tracked as `absolute-diplomatic-snowyowl`. Parity sweep: N/A, this is one pytest-only surface. Residual architecture risk: wholesale replacement of production-side Pandoc calls remains held by ADR 0095; accepted for this ticket. Replication: Gerrit LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, zero unresolved comments; GitHub run 31766586337 passed without retry. Workflow wall was 3,537s because contention delayed macOS start by 1,640s; macOS then ran 1,885s. The repaired existential test disappeared from macOS slowest-25; remaining >30s tests were corpus pass-1 setup 139.37s, loopback editor setup 35.09s, and fixed-point prose 31.01s.
